output.evidence: Both candidates keep the Chrome Vapor Meridian set (brushed steel wall folding into steel ground, single mist band, product small at left, right-column sans typography with peach rule), but version 2 resolves the physical story better: its horizon mist band sits clearly behind the bottle base so the flacon reads as standing in front of the wall-ground junction on a ground plane with perspective-directed brush grain, and a soft contact shadow sinks into that grain, fulfilling the brief's 'contact shadow陷进细拉丝纹'. Version 1's mist band cuts across the bottle's lower body at nearly the same height as its base, flattening the junction and leaving the flacon ambiguously seated, and its ground reads as a mere continuation of the wall texture. Typography in version 2 is equally coherent (wide-tracked PRADA eyebrow, single-line geometric sans title vertically overlapping the cap zone but horizontally separated, peach steam-gauge rule), and the rule resting on the mist band echoes the horizon line intentionally. Product fidelity (triangle silhouette, black lacquer cap, gold collar, peach juice) is intact in both, with no studio equipment or floating-packshot artifacts.
remaining_problems: Title is set in title case ('Paradoxe') rather than the declared geometric all-caps Century Gothic treatment
Peach steam-gauge rule in version 2 sits low on the mist band, slightly weakening its role as a mid-column gauge and reducing contrast against the bright glow
Contact shadow is soft and shallow; the baked-in white luminance of the glass still limits transmission into the cool steel ground
Right column carries only three elements, leaving the upper steel field quiet to the point of emptiness rather than composed negative space
